page: Amazon Web Services r3.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor and powered by an older-generation Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance delivers 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores via hyperthreading, backed by 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 7.62 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 25 MB of L3 cache, standard AVX support, and AES instructions, though it lacks modern instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX. Bundled storage is present in the form of an 80 GB local SSD, and networking is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark results highlight the legacy nature of the Ivy Bridge-EP architecture. In compute testing, the instance achieved 1,272.38 on stress-ng single-core and 3,358.35 on multi-core, with Geekbench scores of 713.0 for single-core and 1,540.0 for multi-core, placing overall CPU performance in the lower percentiles compared to modern platforms. Memory bandwidth benchmarks recorded 26.48 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 22.95 GB/sec for writes, resulting in an average PassMark memory score of 2,088.86. Application-level metrics reflect these limits, registering 1.48 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 3.78 GB/sec throughput for static web serving.

The primary tradeoff of the r3.xlarge is its high memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with legacy computing efficiency. Modern workloads requiring aggressive instruction set optimizations or high computational density will find its compute capacity constrained. However, for memory-resident legacy applications, moderate in-memory caches, small transactional databases, and basic ETL processing that need generous RAM allocations without demanding modern per-core processing throughput, the instance provides functional memory density alongside integrated local scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r3.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration provides 30.0 GB of RAM, an 80 GB local SSD volume, and a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps over a Xen hypervisor. Hardware support covers AVX and AES instructions, but lacks newer AVX-512 and vector extensions. Synthetic and application benchmarks demonstrate modest throughput typical of older x86_64 architectures, marked by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1,540.0, a PassMark memory score of 2,088.86, and 1.48 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. The hardware profile suits legacy in-memory caching, intermediate data manipulation, and lightweight database workloads where high memory capacity is favored over raw processor speed.
